#1817. Thomas Tuchel reveals key reason why England beat Spain in ‘best performance’ of his tenure

Thomas Tuchel has explained why England’s 3-2 win over Spain was the best performance of his tenure.

The German has been in charge of the Three Lions since January 2025 and guided them to third place at the World Cup in the summer, their highest finish in the competition since their only title in 1966.

That included memorable wins against Croatia, DR Congo and Mexico. Last month, in the Nations League, England inflicted upon Croatia the heaviest defeat in their history as they thrashed Slaven Bilic’s side 7-0 in Rijeka.

But Tuchel admitted he views Sunday’s 10-man victory over the world champions in Madrid as the finest performance during his time at the helm.

Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored for the Three Lions as they ended the world champions’ 43-game unbeaten streak despite conceding twice in the second half. It secured England top spot in their Nations League group ahead of Spain.

“Brilliant performance,” Tuchel told ITV after the game. “A well deserved win. Overall we were the better team. Fantastic performance from start to finish.

“It was a complete performance. We brought everything to the table. We were brave. Spirit-wise, energy-wise and also football quality was highest level.

“We deserved it. We focused on our performance and attitude. I can’t praise the team high enough for what they put out there.”

Speaking about how England dug in defensively once Spain had scored their second goal, Tuchel said: “Half an hour feels like two hours against a team like this [with 10 men]. That’s the way it is. Without the red card we were clear winners.”

Asked what England showed, he replied: “What we are made of and what we can do. We are always ready to push our limits. We had our best result in 60 years [at the World Cup] and we weren’t happy with it. It’s impressive what we did in the last two camps.”

#1816. Declan Rice makes bold claim after England’s win over Spain

Declan Rice says the England squad ‘knew’ they would beat World Cup holders Spain in their final Nations League group game.

England earned top spot in their Nations League group and ended Spain’s extraordinary 43-game unbeaten run with a thrilling 3-2 win in Madrid.

Thomas Tuchel’s side scored three goals in 12 minutes either side of half-time to stun Spain before withstanding a late siege to seal their finest win under the German boss.

Harry Kane took his international tally to 93 goals with a penalty on the stroke of half-time as England deservedly ended the opening 45 minutes ahead.

Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White then scored twice in the space of four minutes to open up a commanding 3-0 lead over the shell-shocked Spaniards.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Elliot Anderson’s red card on 63 minutes and Mikel Oyarzabal’s subsequent penalty offered Spain a route back into a match they looked out of.

England fans feared a collapse similar to the one the team suffered in last summer’s World Cup semi-final against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second with 20 minutes remaining.

But this time England kept their opponents at bay with some resolute defending and two superb saves from goalkeeper James Trafford.

Rice was full of praise for his teammates after the Nations League win and said he ‘knew’ England would beat the world champions in their own backyard.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘We knew we were going to beat them tonight,’ Rice told ITV. ‘The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive.

"We knew we were going to beat them tonight!"Declan Rice after England's win over Spain in Madrid 🇪🇸🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 pic.twitter.com/dbNiMi74od

‘Our first ten minutes were probably the best we’ve played. It was pressure, pressure, pressure – we could have had two or three.

‘If we don’t go down to ten men, we see more of the ball, we start to see them jump more, we start to see more space, and we start to see our attacking players thrive like they were doing in the second half.

‘With ten men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against that team is massive. It’s a massive win. Credit to everyone.

‘When they got the second, you might have thought that it was going to go the other way with the amount of pressure they were putting on, but that resilience.

‘Keep emptying the tank, doing anything for this badge, for this team, for our players, for the manager.’

Meanwhile, Tuchel hailed England’s ‘brilliant performance’ after they beat a side who last lost in regulation play in March 2024.

‘Brilliant performance. Well deserved win,’ he said. ‘Overall we were the better team. Fantastic performance from start to finish.

‘It was a long 30 minutes after the red card but I don’t want to focus on that. There were so many positive things in the first 60 minutes.

‘Complete performance. We brought everything to the table. We were brave. Spirit wise, energy wise and also football quality was highest level.

‘We deserved it. We focused on our performance and attitude. I can’t praise the team high enough for what they put out there.’

#1815. CM: Three names on the list as Milan begin difficult hunt for Modric’s heir

AC Milan must start thinking about the midfield of the future, and there are reportedly a few names on the list of ideas.

At 41 years of age Luka Modric, still remains simply irreplaceable for Ruben Amorim and for Milan. However, given that his deal expires at the end of the season, the Rossoneri management have a duty to also look to the future and prepare for the post-Modric era.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The scouting team are very active in England, Spain, Belgium, and France, looking for the right players for Amorim’s footballing philosophy. Among the priorities for next season is identifying the right player to potentially take the reins as a deeper-lying playmaker.

Calciomercato.com report that three players have attracted considerable interest from Milan. One of them is Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, but he remains a dream at the moment because Arsenal and Chelsea have already swooped in on him.

The 23-year-old was called up to the England squad for the last break because manager Thomas Tuchel is very keen on him, but there’s a significant obstacle: the price tag. In England, there is even talk of a €100m+ asking price, given the clubs interested.

The spotlight has recently turned on Brighton’s Yasin Ayari too. He’s a highly versatile midfielder, performing at a high level both as a defensive midfielder and behind the striker. The Swede’s deal runs out in 2027 making him a big opportunity, but Brighton have a one-year option to.

Finally, we arrive at the new name on the list: Adem Zorgane of Union-Saint Gilloise. Scouts like what they have seen from the Algerian, who combines physicality with good technical ability. He would likely be the cheapest of the three, but his potential is high in the eyes of Milan.

#1814. Arsenal ‘left everything on the pitch’ in London City draw, says Slegers

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Renee Slegers lauded Arsenal for "leaving everything out on the pitch" despite being held to a 1-1 draw with London City Lionesses in the Women's Super League.

Arsenal came into this game on the back of earning a 1-1 draw with Barcelona in the Women's Champions League in midweek and started brightly at Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners took the lead through Frida Maanum just 10 minutes in, as she combined with Alessia Russo to get the better of Mary Earps.

But just 98 seconds later, London City were back on level terms through Isobel Goodwin, who netted in front of England boss Sarina Wiegman.

Mary Earps was the standout though, as Arsenal searched in vain for a winner, with Maanum twice thwarted by the goalkeeper, while Caitlin Foord and Lisa Baum also saw chances go begging.

Arsenal got nine of their 17 shots on target, accumulating 1.14 expected goals (xG) and had three Opta-defined 'big' chances, but are still without a home win in the WSL this term.

Slegers, however, was thrilled with what she saw from her team in her 50th WSL game in charge.

"Two good teams going against each other," Slegers told Sky Sports. "We started the game well, scored a very good goal, but we let them back into the game too easily.

"We spent more time than we normally do without the ball, partly [because of] the game plan and also the questions they were asking us. We created big chances and could have done more with the chances to get the win; that's the frustrating part.

"We had the biggest crowd so far at the Emirates. We couldn't get the win, but they [the fans] have been so big for us.

Fought until the end, but it ends all square. https://t.co/Zgns4EHYfw

— Arsenal Women (@ArsenalWFC) November 15, 2026

"I want to recognise the effort from the fans coming out. Unfortunately, we couldn't do it for them again.

"The players left everything on the pitch; they were absolutely dedicated. Playing with hunger and focus.

"There are things in our game we need to do better: spend less energy without the ball. We want to dominate the ball but also defend well and use spaces when they are there. Be more ruthless and create more chances going forward."

London City have made no secret of their desire to qualify for the Champions League, and they showed off their credentials once again at Emirates Stadium.

They sit third in the WSL, just six points behind leaders Chelsea, while they are six points ahead of Arsenal, who are three places below them.

While Delphine Cascarino hit the woodwork from London City's best chance to take all three points, they were indebted to Earps, who made eight saves and four clearances – only Jana Fernandez made more (five).

"Mary is a very strong character and is much more than the things we see in terms of the performance," said Eder Maestre.

"She has experience and energy that you can bring to every part in the process and not just the things we see in the matches.

"I think the energy that she brings to the position is massive and has a massive impact. I'm very pleased with her."

At the other end of the table, Charlton Athletic became the first side in WSL history to lose their opening 10 matches of a campaign after their 2-0 defeat to West Ham, who moved up to ninth.

Aston Villa also earned derby bragging rights after edging past Birmingham City 1-0 earlier on Sunday.

#1813. Michael Carrick facing the sack at Man United: Mauricio Pochettino the frontrunner to replace beleaguered boss - but chiefs face splashing out £7MILLION for former Spurs and Chelsea coach

Published: 18:04 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 02:44 EST, 10 November 2026

Michael Carrick is facing the sack with Manchester United bosses leaning towards installing a new head coach during the international break.

Carrick’s position has become increasingly precarious after United dropped into the relegation zone despite salvaging a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

It left the 45-year-old with just one win from 10 Premier League games this season – United’s worst start since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago.

Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as a new frontrunner to replace Carrick. The Argentine is currently in charge of the US national team, but his contract includes a £7million release clause.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, who were both under consideration when United gave Carrick more time to turn the season around following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth last month, could also be in contention.

In the three games since then, Carrick’s side lost at Chelsea, staged a remarkable comeback to beat Roma in the Champions League in midweek and then fought back again to draw with Villa.

Michael Carrick is likely to be sacked from his role as Manchester United manager during the international break

It is understood that United officials have not made a final decision, though there is expectation that there will be a new boss in place after the international break

Although it’s understood that no final decision has been reached over Carrick’s future and insiders say that speculation over his sacking is premature, the expectation within Old Trafford is that a new man will be in charge for the visit to Anfield a week on Sunday.

Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January and the former United midfielder was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

But this season has unravelled alarmingly for United with his three wins in 15 games in all competitions coming at home to newly-promoted Ipswich in the Premier League as well as Sabah of Azerbaijan and Roma in the Champions League.

Asked after Sunday’s chaotic draw with Villa if he would consider quitting, a defiant Carrick said: ‘That's not going to happen.

‘We’re in November. I don’t like this situation and where we are. But we can do something about it. I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it's got to win games.’

Sacking Carrick would leave United searching for their eighth permanent manager or head coach since Ferguson retired 13-and-a-half years ago.

Pochettino was strongly linked with the job when Erik ten Hag was appointed in 2022 and again when the Dutchman was sacked two years later.

The 54-year-old has extensive Premier League experience at Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton and was also in charge at Paris Saint-Germain.

Current US boss - and former Tottenham and Chelsea manager - Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the frontrunner to replace Carrick

Howe was previously seen as the favourite but it’s understood there has been no contact between United and the former Newcastle boss.

It would cost United around £3million in compensation to appoint the 48-year-old under the terms of his departure from St James’s Park in July.

Nagelsmann is available after leaving his role as head coach of the German national team in the summer when they were eliminated from the World Cup following a penalty shootout defeat by Paraguay in the round of 32.

#1812. Sudan vs Senegal - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 14 Nov 2026 06:19, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 16:27

Sudan will be looking to bounce back from a heavy defeat in Dakar when they welcome Senegal to the Juba National Stadium on Monday.

The Lions of Teranga sit top of Group J on seven points from three games after Thursday’s 4-1 win in the reverse fixture, while the hosts are third on three points, having won one and lost two of their opening three qualifiers.

Senegal have made an unbeaten start to life under Patrick Vieira, who replaced Pape Thiaw after the Lions were eliminated by Belgium in the last 32 of the 2026 World Cup.

They opened with a 1-1 draw away to Mozambique, with Nicolas Jackson scoring, then won 1-0 away to Ethiopia thanks to Ibrahim Mbaye’s early goal.

Thursday’s victory in Dakar was Vieira’s home debut and it went smoothly, with the in-form Jackson putting Senegal ahead in the 31st minute, before they scored three times in 25 second-half minutes to take the game away after Mohamed Abuaagla equalised on 45 minutes.

The Lions will hope for the same on Monday and will be quite optimistic, having never lost to Sudan in nine meetings across all competitions.

Sudan, ranked 118th in the world against Senegal’s 18th, began with a 1-0 win over Ethiopia in Juba, where Mohamed Eisa scored a penalty in the 86th minute.

They then lost 4-1 away to Mozambique, with Yasin Hamed’s penalty in the 88th minute their only goal. Abuaagla’s equaliser on Thursday came after both of their previous goals in the campaign had been penalties.

They have now conceded four goals in each of their last two games, a lack of defensive solidity that will be a big issue for coach James Kwesi Appiah, especially given that the two wins they have recorded in their last nine games have had to come with clean sheets.

However, they will hope to withstand the arsenal in Senegal’s attack, though the Falcons of Jediane might find that difficult due to fatigue, having taken a long route to this fixture, as Juba, in South Sudan, is their designated home ground in this campaign.

Sudan Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Senegal Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Sudan named a 24-man squad for the double-header, with several of Kwesi Appiah's players coming from domestic heavyweights Al Hilal and Al Merrikh.

Mohamed Eisa, Yasir Mozamil and Abubakr Eisa are among the attacking options available to Appiah, while defenders Ahmed Tabanja and Mustafa Karshom and goalkeeper Mohamed Mustafa will be important to the visitors' hopes of keeping Senegal at bay.

Senegal are without several regulars, with Sadio Mane and Idrissa Gana Gueye left out of Vieira's squad, while Ismail Jakobs has retired from international football after announcing his decision in October.

Krepin Diatta was initially selected but subsequently became unavailable through injury and replaced by Sevilla defender Arouna Sangante, while Mamadou Sarr is also sidelined with a calf problem.

Habib Diarra, Ismaila Sarr and Abdallah Sima are also unavailable for medical reasons.

Vieira can call upon Aston Villa duo Jackson and Mbaye in attack, with Boulaye Dia, Iliman Ndiaye and the newly called-up Pathe Mboup also providing options in the final third.

Kalidou Koulibaly captains the side, while Dion Lopy has returned after missing the previous international window.

Mustafa; Awad, Tabanja, Karshoum, Kuku; Khidir, Abuaagla; Alhassan, Omer, Nooh; Eisa

Diouf; Sane, Koulibaly, Niakhate; Mbaye, Camara, Lopy, El Hadji Malick Diouf; Ndiaye, Dia, Jackson

Sudan have conceded eight goals in two games and such porosity will be punished severely against a Senegal side that has a clear edge in quality and depth.

The Lions should have enough to win again and move to 10 points, and this should be a straightforward one, though we expect the scoreline to be more respectable compared to the reverse fixture.

#1811. Why Chelsea aren't European contenders, Tottenham aren't 'back'... and Brighton and Bournemouth are in a title race: What you should believe and what's just a mirage after 10 Premier League games - and the proof behind it

Published: 12:18 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 03:11 EST, 10 November 2026

We are ten games into the Premier League season and another international break provides the ideal opportunity to take stock on what has been a bewildering start to another campaign.

Michael Carrick heads off for a couple of weeks with Manchester United still in the bottom three. Brighton perch second in the Premier League behind Arsenal, who are threatening to run away with it. Tottenham are only a point outside the top half, which is enough on its own to make you squint and rub your eyes. That can’t be right.

We are more than a quarter of the way through now, enough time for patterns to emerge and directions of travel to settle but also not long enough for us to be entirely sure who’s still benefitting from an early hot streak or suffering from unfair misfortune.

Who is where they belong? What can we believe? Daily Mail Sport digs into the numbers to figure out what’s real and what is fake about this Premier League season so far...

REAL: Defences CAN win you titles, just ask Arsenal

Sir Alex Ferguson was wrong, of course, when he declared that ‘attack wins you games, defence wins you titles’. Over the 31 completed 20-team Premier League seasons, fewer than half of them were won by the team that conceded the fewest goals. More than two thirds of them, however, were won by the side that scored the most.

Sometimes, as was often the case during the Pep Guardiola era, teams can be the best at both. Of the 15 times since 1995-96 that the best defence triumphed, they were also the most prolific attack on nine occasions.

Arsenal's goals, xG, shots and shots on target are all at their lowest per game since Mikel Arteta’s first season in charge. But thanks to their defence, they are five points clear at the top

Arsenal, however, are certainly not that. Their title win last season was only the sixth time in the previous 30 years that the best defence alone was crowned champions. They are doing it again this season, five points clear and proving that the best defence can still win you a title on its own.

And it’s a good job, too, because while their defence is as rock-solid as ever, their attack is getting worse. Last season, the Gunners ranked second for goals but fourth for expected goals (xG) and shots. This term, they are sixth for goals, fifth for xG and 10th for shots.

Their goals, xG, shots and shots on target are all at their lowest per game since Arteta’s first season in charge. Their win over Hull was their fourth 1-0 victory of the campaign. Not that Arteta will care. His defence means they still have the best xG difference in the division and it’s going to win him another league title.

That euphoric 3-1 victory over Manchester City was coming. There had been a fair amount of noise building around Oliver Glasner’s start to life on the Trent as Nottingham Forest went into the weekend second from bottom in the Premier League.

One defeat in nine. Was it Glasner’s new system taking time to bed in like it did at Crystal Palace? How quickly would ‘Mr Marinakis’ lose his patience this time around and fire another head coach?

This time last year, Forest were already on to their third manager of the season. Patience, for once, will reap its rewards. Forest didn’t deserve to be 19th. They have the fifth-best expected goal difference in the division. When you dig into the numbers, Forest have the best defence of any team not named Arsenal.

Fewest shots faced, second-fewest shots on target faced after the Gunners, second lowest xG conceded after, yep, Arsenal. They have made the fewest errors leading to shots all season with just two. Bournemouth are next on five.

Their problem is they, somehow, have not been able to score. Only Sunderland – another side doing worse than their expected numbers would suggest – have underperformed their xG in front of goal more than Forest. I was at Crystal Palace for Glasner’s return to Selhurst Park and, quite simply, Forest should have been 4-0 up by half-time.

They have the lowest shot conversion rate of any side in the league at just 5.5 per cent. That’s unsustainably low. Only one team since 2014-15 has maintained one as low as that across an entire season and that was Huddersfield in 2018-19, when they finished bottom with 16 points. Forest are nowhere near that bad.

Their need for a striker has long been obvious and if Liam Delap’s brace against City can spark some confidence and form, they might have the striker they need to start climbing up the table and, who knows, into European contention.

Nottingham Forest will hope Liam Delap's brilliant brace against Manchester City is the start of them getting past their woes in front of goal

Listen to Jamie O’Hara on talkSPORT after a run of three wins on the trot, and he might have you believing that Spurs are back.

Along with another defeat, this time to Leeds, to bring Spurs hurtling to earth, their numbers simply are not good enough – and certainly not in attack – to be deemed as such.

They may have attempted the fifth-most shots in the division but in doing so have still put up the fourth-worst xG, as their xG per shot is the worst in the division. In short: they shoot a lot but hardly ever from anywhere dangerous. That 40 per cent of their goals have come from outside the box, the highest in the league, is unsustainable.

They just don’t create enough. Left back Andy Robertson has created the most chances for Spurs this season with 14. Twenty-seven players have created more than him so far, with 15 other clubs boasting at least one star higher than Tottenham’s top man. Sunderland have two above him and Arsenal, Brighton and Manchester United have three.

Tottenham have the worst xG per shot in the league - meaning they rarely get into good positions to score

REAL: Brighton (and maybe Bournemouth) are in a title race

We have got used to seeing these modest but exceptionally run clubs punching above their weight in the Premier League but even the most appreciative of us could not have expected to see at least one of them in a title race.

If, by title race, we mean the team that might get closest to Arsenal. Looking at the underlying numbers, it could even be both of them.

When you look at the expected goal difference of all clubs in the division – those you should have scored from the quality of the chances you create, against those you should have conceded from the quality of the ones you allow your opponents to create – Bournemouth and Brighton sit behind only Arsenal and Man City.

Brighton are the division’s top scorers by a distance, five more than anyone else, but even though they are outperforming their expected numbers (their players can’t keep scoring one in every 10 shots they take from outside the box – looking at you, Diego Gomez) the Seagulls are still putting up the second biggest xG behind City.

Of the 11 players to create more than 20 chances so far, Brighton are the only side to have two names in there in Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. They also, of course, beat Arsenal and City without conceding to either team.

They do need to get tighter at the back if they wish to stay near the top, mind. Brighton should have conceded about seven more goals than they have done. No side has overperformed their defensive data quite so much.

Bournemouth are the ones who should be doing better, which sounds mad for a team that’s just won eight games on the bounce in less than a month in all competitions. The Cherries sit seventh but have the third-best xG, and the third-best xG conceded. That, no matter how you look at it, is a recipe for prolonged success.

Brighton's Diego Gomez can't continue scoring every shot he has from long range... can he?

Bournemouth are the ones who should be doing better, which sounds mad for a team that’s just won eight games on the bounce in less than a month

Speaking of overperforming, few teams are doing quite so well to hide their abundant flaws as Chelsea. Xabi Alonso’s side sit fifth in the Premier League and the Spaniard can be thankful to the football gods for it. They should not be fifth.

Chelsea sit in the bottom half for both xG for and against. Their expected goal difference puts them in 14th, below Fulham, Manchester United and Sunderland.

Only Brighton have scored more goals than they should have done based on their chances but, unlike the Seagulls, Chelsea’s baseline is far more mediocre. Opta’s expected points table has them 12th.

They are also one of only two sides in the division this season not to have had a single goal scored by a substitute.

Chelsea's expected goal difference puts them in 14th, below Fulham, Manchester United and Sunderland

When you lose a manager as influential as Eddie Howe, it’s always going to be a tricky transition. When you sell Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon and struggle to replace them adequately, it’s going to be harder still.

Still, Newcastle should be doing better. They should not be creating better chances than only Hull and Coventry. Their expected goal difference is only better than Coventry, Ipswich and Palace. Opta’s expected table has them just outside the relegation zone.

Only three teams have faced more shots, only three have attempted more shots on target, only five have played fewer passes into the box.

Daily Mail Sport revealed last week that Newcastle’s players are ‘confused’ by new manager Matthias Jaissle’s instructions, playing style and strategy. Jaissle accused his team after the defeat to Everton of not following his instructions or executing the tactics they had worked on in training.

They have to find a way of getting it to click after the international break otherwise they will be fighting out most of their season closer to that dotted line.

It can often be fun for supporters of other clubs around the country to revel in the pain and misery that Manchester United appear intent on inflicting on their own supporters.

Even the carnage and chaos of coming from two goals down against Aston Villa and the shot of joy that can bring was still only enough to leave United 18th in the table.

Do they deserve to be there? With just one win all season, the fewest in the league, you would think so. United have, perhaps, not quite been that bad – but they certainly don’t help themselves.

Everyone talks about them having tons of shots, which they do. They have had the most in the division by a distance, which always keeps the xG totting up, but so many of them come from miles away. United, too often, take the scattergun approach.

Manchester United have been suffering from bad luck at the back - but will it correct itself in time to save them from a relegation battle?

Their xG per shot is the lowest in the division, meaning their shots aren’t from dangerous positions, and their conversion rate is one of the worst, too. When 45 per cent of your attempts on goal come from outside the box, that’s likely to happen. That makes their midtable expected goal difference slightly misleading.

Their main problem is at the back – and that is where they are being consistently punished. It is the opposite story to their attack.

United have faced among the fewest shots in the division but among the most on target. Their xG per shot faced is the highest in the league, and their opponents enjoy a higher conversion rate than against any other team.

That, though, is unlikely to remain sustainable. They are unlikely to keep getting punished quite so harshly. That should be enough to drag them clear – but only just.

#1808. Arsenal news: Max Dowman breaks another record on historic England appearance

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 09:17

Arsenal teenager Max Dowman made another piece of history when he represented England Under-21s on Friday night.

Despite recent criticism from Gunners boss Mikel Arteta, the 16-year-old continues to be fast-tracked for both club and country.

As well as already making 19 appearances for Arsenal's first team, the winger has made an array of appearances for England at youth level.

Dowman had already earned 13 caps for England at Under-19 level before being handed a call-up to Lee Carsley's Under-21 squad for the November international break.

That gave Dowman the chance to make history versus Portugal on Friday night.

Carsley named Dowman on the substitutes' bench for the showdown at Ashton Gate.

A first-half goal from Afonso Moreira made the difference as Portugal earned a 1-0 victory at the home of Championship club Bristol City.

However, Dowman became the youngest ever representative of England Under-21s when he was introduced as a 61st-minute substitute.

Jude Bellingham had previously held the feat for six years, having made his debut aged 17 years, two months and six days when facing Kosovo in 2020.

In comparison, Dowman featured on Friday night aged 16 years, 10 months and 13 days.

Dowman will now hope to be handed his first England Under-21s start when France are the opponents on Monday night.

As he is still serving a domestic ban, Dowman remains suspended for Arsenal's Premier League game at Newcastle United on November 21.

However, he is expected to be part of the squad for the Champions League encounter versus Borussia Dortmund on November 24.

#1807. Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

They wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

“In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This shows how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland said. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the big stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”

For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS

Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”

36 - Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.Inevitability. pic.twitter.com/HHbNadybxh

“I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. The fans have been absolutely brilliant and this is a new step in my career. Erling [Haaland] is an animal, a beast. Every time I am on the pitch, I will look for him and look to assist him. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”

“Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

“He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”

AEK Athens 1 LASK 0 Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 Dortmund 3 Villarreal 2 Lille 2 Real Betis 3 Porto 0 Manchester City 2 Real Madrid 2 Inter Milan 1

The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

Enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

That is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

Haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

Whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

That is a big chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

Porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

For the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

Ndiaye receives it out on the left before driving inside. He gets his shot away from the edge of the box and tries to pick out the far corner but it is too close to D Costa and an easy save for the Porto keeper.

A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

Enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

Varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

That was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

Just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was embracing Daniel Sturridge in the press box and they weren’t in their seats when the goal went in. Lovely move from City and Haaland steered in his 58th goal in the competition.

Erling Haaland moves 7th in the ALL-TIME UCL top-scorers list 💪🇳🇴📊 pic.twitter.com/oIkrPxm0gT

Haaland wasted two headed opportunities in the first half but he does not spurn this chance. It is a first Manchester City assist for Enzo, who clips in a cross from the left side of the box. Haaland meets it and his header glances off the far post and goes in.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

Gabriel Clarke on Amazon Prime has reported that there was some trouble in the tunnel as the two sides went off for half-time. Both sets of security teams for the clubs were forced to step in.

We are back under way in Porto. Tempers were really starting to boil over as that first half wore on so will that continue into the second half?

The former Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea striker has described the incident involving Marc Guehi and Gabri Veiga as a “nasty collision” and “it does not look good at all”. I think Guehi is a lucky man to still be on the pitch as some VAR officials would surely have recommended a review for that foul. Porto boss Francesco Farioli felt Guehi led with his elbow and the home fans were not happy with that as well as a number of other decisions in that first half.

All the stats are massively in Manchester City’s favour but the important statistic, the scoreline, remains level.

The first half is brought to an end and tempers are flaring as the two sides head off, with the game level at 0-0 at the break. The Porto fans and players are not happy with the officiating and Enzo is also involved in some antics.

Gvardiol needs to be careful as he is not punished for delaying a restart when you consider he is already on a booking. The Porto fans want to see a second yellow but the referee says the ball was moving so Porto could not take the restart.

Three added minutes to conclude this first half.

Should Guehi be in trouble here? He appears in real time to win his header but when you watch the replays he led with his arm. He catches Veiga right in the face and Guehi could be in some strife. However, VAR is not going to take any further action and Guehi can count himself lucky. The medics are on to tend to Veiga and you do wonder why VAR has not recommended a review. The ridiculous thing about that was that Guehi was not punished with a yellow card or even a free-kick. That clearly shows the referee did not properly see it.

Porto fans quick to remind Ruben Dias and Enzo Fernandez of their Benfica history. They jeered the pair when they got on the ball. Enzo is getting it from all angles at the moment, with Coventry fans taunting him at the weekend. He can expect more of that in the Premier League after his part in England’s exit at the World Cup, which led to Argentina players holding up a flag saying the Falkland Islands were Argentina’s.

Tensions are boiling over. They have been threatening to do so between Gomes and Gvardiol for a little while and now they do. Gomes steals the ball off Gvardiol and attempts to counter but is pulled back by Gvardiol, who is rightly booked. Gomes is not happy with Gvardiol and they come to blows.

D Costa twice denies Manchester City in a matter of seconds. First he saves from Haaland, then gets to his feet to deny Cherki. Manchester City are knocking on the door and you do feel like a goal is coming for Enzo Maresca’s side.

No goals in Porto but Real Madrid have their second at home against Inter Milan through Fede Valverde.

Manchester City struggled to carve out any genuine chances in the opening quarter of an hour but there are creating more and more opportunities, the latest falling to Foden, whose shot from the right side of the box looking for the far corner is saved by D Costa.

It is not often you see Haaland miss two good chances with his head in quick succession but that is what has happened. Semenyo cuts inside on the left onto his right and curls in a cross into a good area. He picks out Haaland but the Norwegian’s header misses the target. He knows he should have done better as he shakes his head in frustration.

Porto’s front three have struggled to have much of an impact in the game, in particular Silva up top, who has been almost non-existent.

A great save from D Costa to deny Haaland. Foden’s cross just before the byline on the left side of the box picks out Haaland. The Norwegian has barely touched the ball tonight but comes close to opening the scoring. However, D Costa is on hand to deny him with a fine save. Should Haaland have given D Costa the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Diogo Costa CLAWS away Erling Haaland's header 🧤Man City come closest so far in Porto 👀 pic.twitter.com/KVnBHdbNlH

In probably the marquee match-up of the night, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are taking on Inter Milan at the Bernabeu. Real have just taken the lead through Kylian Mbappe.

Semenyo cuts inside from the left and gets a shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at D Costa. That was Manchester City’s first shot of the night.

Veiga has a shot saved at the near post by Donnarumma but the offside flag goes up. Veiga and Pep exchange a neat one-two down Porto’s left before Veiga’s effort is saved but Pepe was offside in the build-up.

Manchester City are dominating possession and perhaps it was a ploy by Enzo Marecsa to take it slowly and hog the ball in order to take the early sting out of Porto. The visitors would have been expecting the hosts would want to start hot so maybe they were willing to be slow on the ball in order to quieten down the crowd early doors. They have not had a shot yet and not really threatened the Porto goal but the hosts have not offered much going forward.

The weather in Porto really is horrible, the type of weather you would expect in Manchester in mid-November than Porto in early September.

Porto have a strong defensive record thus far this season but undoubtedly they will be tested a lot more tonight than they are in Liga Portugal. You would also imagine they will have to be clinical in attack as they are unlikely to create as many chances as they do domestically.

With it hammering down, Porto boss Francesco Farioli has swapped his lovely suit that he was wearing pre-game for a tracksuit top and cap. At half-time, he will probably head back in drenched like all the players if he is active in his dugout.

We are under way at the Estádio do Dragão with the rain still teaming down in Porto. Manchester City’s Champions League campaign gets going.

It has been pouring down in Porto but that has not dampened the spirits of the home fans, who are in fine voice ahead of kick-off. The pyrotechnics have gone off and it is loud inside the Dragão. Both sides then emerge from the tunnel and here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

It has been a decent day for Phil Foden already. The City forward’s race horse, Wreck It Ronnie, won at Goodwood and set a new record in the sport. The horse named after his son defeated Najidi Storm, which was started the race with 1-33 odds. It means the favourite is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. Foden’s family also call him “Ronnie”, which is the name he gave his son.

The Polish referee was branded a “Madridista” last year after being pictured with a Real wash bag in the dressing room. Barcelona were unhappy with this after he took charge of a clash against Inter Milan which ended in an epic defeat.

Aston Villa have held on to beat Club Brugge 3-2 and you can catch all the reaction to that game right here.

The big news here at Estádio do Dragão is that Ayyoub Bouaddi is given his full Manchester City debut, after coming off the bench in previous Premier League games. The Morocco midfielder, 18, starts in midfield in place of Elliot Anderson from the team that defeated Coventry at the weekend. Phil Foden is also given the nod, replacing Iliman Ndiaye.

The Opta Supercomputer, before a ball was kicked tonight, has produced these numbers for what it thinks about who might win the Champions League this season:

The Argentine started for Manchester City on Saturday against Coventry and he once more takes a place in the centre of their midfield tonight. He starts alongside Ayyoub Bouaddi to form a £200m+ starting midfield pairing.

Aston Villa are into the second half of their game over at Club Brugge. As they kicked off in the second half, Villa were 3-1 up but Brugge have got a goal back. It could be a nervy finish for Unai Emery’s side and you can follow the conclusion of that match right here.

In the forward line for Porto tonight is Brazilian winger William Gomes. It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

#1806. Inside the world of Captain Chaos at Man United: Michael Carrick will not walk away but here's what the players are saying as they fail to respond to his direction, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 02:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 03:22 EST, 10 November 2026

While the Manchester United fans who had gone ahead with a booze boycott of Old Trafford watched in horror as their team teetered on the brink of total collapse and head coach Michael Carrick clung to his job, you couldn't help but think of Lloyd Bridges as Steve McCroskey, the frazzled air traffic control boss in Airplane! 'Looks like I picked the wrong week to quit drinking!'

God knows United have forced their supporters to hit the bottle this season, not least in the past six days when they have handed a two-goal advantage to Roma and Aston Villa (twice) and still managed to salvage a win and a draw.

But this cannot carry on. As cavalier as United like to be, this is not the way to play football.

Coming out swinging every game like a boxer on his last legs is great for entertainment, it's great for the Sky Sports cameras beaming it live and the Amazon Prime documentary makers filming behind the scenes, but it is not evidence of solid preparation on the training pitch.

Nowhere in the UEFA coaching manuals will you find a chapter on routinely conceding the first two goals being a sensible route to success. For all his bluster after a bonkers 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, Carrick knows it and his players know it.

'After we concede goals we show character, but if we do this before we can win much more games,' said Matheus Cunha. 'I don't know why, everyone tries to get answers for that. We want to be the best and show that we can come back. We need to show the mentality to do this from the start.'

As Manchester United head coach, Michael Carrick is doing a convincing impersonation of Captain Chaos

Coming out swinging every game like a boxer on his last legs is great for entertainment, but it is not evidence of solid preparation on the training pitch

It isn't just in the last week either. United were a goal down against Atletico Madrid inside the first minute and Como in the second. They were two down to Villa after three minutes and 40 seconds, the earliest that has happened to United in the Premier League era.

This is not a coincidence. It is not bad luck. This is in the mind-set of these Manchester United players, and the game management of Carrick – and that is what should worry Old Trafford bosses the most.

As if being in the relegation zone for the next two weeks after a start of one win from 10 games – the worst since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago – is not bad enough, United don't seem to be playing to a plan. They are not responding to direction. They are reverting to instinct and moments of skill when everything else fails.

Carrick made reference to it when he spoke before this game, admitting that the players are better when they don't think too much.

'Momentum within games, day-to-day, week-to-week, game-to-game, it's huge,' he said at Carrington on Friday. 'I think it's important with your feelings and your emotions to roll with it. Then your memory can click in and you realise, 'Oh yeah, this is what it feels like, this is how it should be', and you start seeing different things.

'It's all got to come together, but feeling, confidence, and that emotion and sometimes not even thinking. You're at your best when you don't think too much and you just trust and play on instinct, and I think we did a lot of that the other night (against Roma).'

The irony is that Carrick was so measured, so composed as a player. Now, as coach, he is doing a convincing impersonation of Captain Chaos. United's games are reminiscent of the high-scoring madness of Erik ten Hag's last full season in charge, devoid of stability or structure.

That is what Carrick's employers need to consider when they sit down to discuss whether he can restore the sanity of his first four months in charge which guided the club towards third place and Champions League qualification.

Now they are third from bottom and will stay in the relegation zone for the duration of the international break. For three minutes on Sunday, Manchester United – the aristocrats of English football – were actually in last place after Sunderland took the lead against Chelsea and Crystal Palace were still goalless with Liverpool.

United don't seem to be playing to a plan or responding to direction - they are reverting to instinct and moments of skill when everything else fails

Carrick's employers need to consider  whether he can restore the sanity of his first four months in charge

That being in 18th place – one below Coventry – is somehow seen as blessed relief from the unrelenting humiliation of this season, says everything about the state of the club.

At the end of a week that marked 40 years since Ferguson's arrival and was celebrated by a dinner with many of his most famous players, it has been quite the fall from grace.

Which brings us back to the fans. They are a loyal bunch and once again serenaded Carrick off the pitch at full-time having spent much of the previous two hours slaughtering the owners, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Protest groups had urged them to boycott buying alcohol at the stadium to hit the Glazer family and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in the pocket. 'Your funeral not ours – sell up now,' read one new banner. 'We don't want a new stadium, we want new owners,' said another.

But they know their football at United. Was it support or just sympathy with a head coach who has done his best in an impossible situation?

Carrick says he won't walk away and they never do. On Remembrance Sunday, he stood there on the touchline with a poppy on his arm and hope in his heart that United could get themselves out of another self-inflicted crisis.

They did. Again. But how much longer can United and Carrick keep winging it, and believe that calm will emerge from the chaos.

#1805. Christian Imga: Athletic Bilbao's £75m clause after 15 clubs show interest

By Naim Beneddra | 14 Nov 2026 09:32

Athletic Bilbao have moved to protect one of their most promising young talents with a new long-term contract featuring a release clause that could eventually reach £75m, following reported interest from 15 Champions League clubs.

The player in question is Christian Imga, a 17-year-old winger whose rapid emergence from the Basque club's academy has already earned him opportunities under former Borussia Dortmund manager Edin Terzic.

Athletic confirmed on November 8 that Imga had signed a contract until June 2031, with an option for the club to extend the agreement by another season.

According to Spanish radio station Cadena SER, representatives of the youngster have revealed that as many as 15 clubs competing in the Champions League have enquired about his availability and contractual situation in recent months.

The interest reportedly prompted Athletic sporting director Mikel Gonzalez to accelerate negotiations, resulting in a considerably improved agreement designed to discourage potential suitors.

Imga's release clause is understood to increase progressively, potentially reaching €85m (£75m) towards the end of his contract, although the amount required to sign him immediately would be lower.

Imga's representatives have confirmed that the teenager's progress has attracted attention from several of Europe's leading teams, including clubs from Spain.

"There have been many clubs asking about Cristian. Many top European clubs," a representative told Cadena SER's Bilbao sports programme.

"In terms of interest, clubs asking about him and his contractual conditions, we could say 15 Champions League clubs. Almost everyone has made enquiries."

The identities of those clubs have not been disclosed, and there is no indication that Athletic have received 15 formal transfer offers.

Nevertheless, the level of attention surrounding a player who only made his senior debut last month helps explain the club's determination to secure his future.

Spanish newspaper AS reports that the release clause could rise from approximately €70m (£61m) to €85m (£75m) over the course of the agreement. Cadena SER, meanwhile, suggests that the initial figure could be closer to €60m (£52m), with the maximum amount applying if Athletic activate their option to extend the contract.

Athletic's official announcement did not disclose the financial details, but confirmed that the winger had committed his future to the club until at least 2031.

Imga arrived at Lezama from Deportivo Alaves during the 2024-25 season, having experienced a difficult final period with his former club. The youngster was left out of Alaves' youth-team plans after declining a proposed contract extension while negotiations with Athletic were taking place.

His subsequent move to Bilbao initially brought further complications, with competition regulations preventing him from immediately representing his new club's youth side.

Those setbacks have done little to slow his development.

Last season, Imga scored eight goals in 24 appearances for Athletic's Under-18s and added two more in six UEFA Youth League matches.

His performances persuaded the club to promote him directly into Bilbao Athletic, bypassing the usual intermediate step through Basconia.

Standing almost 6ft 3in, Imga is an unusually imposing winger for his age, combining his physical presence with acceleration and the ability to beat defenders in tight spaces.

Although naturally left-footed, he generally operates from the left flank and has shown the versatility to attack both the outside and inside channels.

His progress has particularly impressed Terzic, who has already begun incorporating him into Athletic's senior squad.

The teenager made his first-team debut on October 25, replacing Nico Williams during a 4-0 La Liga victory over Getafe at San Mames.

Four days later, he scored his first senior goal in the Copa del Rey against AE Prat, providing another indication of his readiness to compete above youth level.

Imga's representatives have suggested that his promotion has happened more quickly than originally anticipated because of Terzic's enthusiasm for the youngster.

"The intention was for him to play for Bilbao Athletic this season, but the manager wants to use him whenever he sees him in training," they explained to Cadena SER.

"If things are moving faster, it's because the coach likes him and the player is earning it through his performances."

The teenager has also been selected to represent Spain at the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar, giving him an opportunity to continue his development on the international stage.

He is expected to divide his time between Athletic's reserve team and the senior squad during the remainder of the campaign.

With his new contract secured, Athletic can manage that progression without immediately confronting the prospect of losing him to one of the European clubs reportedly monitoring his performances.

For Imga, the next challenge is to turn his promising first appearances under Terzic into a more regular role at San Mames.

Verdict: Flamengo to score in both halves

#1802. Rio Ferdinand claps back at fans mocking him for celebrating Man United's late equaliser against Aston Villa which left them in the relegation zone

Published: 14:15 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 04:16 EST, 10 November 2026

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at football fans who criticised his reaction on social media to Manchester United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Former United defender Ferdinand drew criticism when he shared a photo of himself celebrating after the Red Devils' dramatic comeback on Sunday afternoon.

Michael Carrick's side had looked down and out at 4-2 in stoppage time, but late strikes from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu meant they earned a point from the game.

They did, though, remain in the relegation zone – however Ferdinand shared two snaps to his X account following full-time.

The first showed the 48-year-old with his head in his hands, and the second saw him celebrating. He captioned the post: 'From this to THIS!!! Carrick time!!!!!!!!!! Birthday weekend just got (a) tad better in the last 6 minutes…'

Fans though flooded the replies with criticism, questioning why he was 'celebrating a draw' and calling him an 'embarrassment'. Ferdinand, though, has now taken the opportunity to respond.

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at fans who criticised his response to Manchester United's draw with Aston Villa

'Let me just address something,' Ferdinand began on Rio Ferdinand Presents. 'On socials I put a picture up and little comment underneath of me going like that (celebrates).

'That's not me celebrating a point against Aston Villa, by the way, it's me celebrating a moment in a football match. It's what football does to you. It can take over your body, take over your emotions in a moment. That moment isn't the big picture.

'So all of these people saying his standards have dropped and he's celebrating a draw... I'm not celebrating a draw against Villa, I'm celebrating the moment and the fact we actually came back and showed a bit of character.

'It's always about that moment that when you calm down and you go, look where we are in the league, that's terrible, looks how things unfolded in the game, that needs work. But, in the moment, as a football fan, you are allowed to get carried away with it.

'That's what football does. If you don't know that or don't understand it or feel it, you're not a football person, so get out.'

Ferdinand hasn't shied away from criticising his former team-mate Carrick amid United's poor run of form that has left them in 18th in the Premier League table.

United came back from behind to draw 4-4 with Villa having looked down and out in the game

His assessment of Sunday's showing was more tame, with the ex-centre back describing the effort as full of both character and chaos.

He added: 'It's like we need a punch on the nose, or two or three, to start playing. But then, the flip side of it, it's character and ability plays a part in that.

'In the end, we could have won it. But they are giving us fans grey hairs. It's crazy football.'

As thrilling as Man United's fight-back may have been to some fans, manager Carrick was still forced to answer difficult questions at full-time.

Sky Sports' Patrick Davison asked the former captain what he 'expected to happen over the next few weeks' - suggesting a question mark still lingering over his tenure despite comebacks against Roma and Villa.

Carrick's response was understandably thorny, with the manager underlining that he 'probably' would not be walking away from the role.

With United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands, Davison pushed further asking: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'

This prompted Carrick to quizzically state: 'Is there?' as the pair engaged in a back-and-forth on the subject.

Eventually Carrick replied: 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

United's start of one win in 10 games is still their worst since Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago this week.

#1800. De la Fuente has ‘nothing but pride and gratitude’ for Spain despite unbeaten run ending

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Luis de la Fuente insists he has "nothing but words of pride and gratitude" for his players as Spain's incredible 43-match unbeaten run came to an end on Sunday.

The reigning world champions were defeated 3-2 by 10-man England at the Metropolitano in the Nations League, meaning they finished second in Group A3, having already qualified for the quarter-finals due to their perfect record before this game.

Harry Kane put the visitors ahead from 12 yards out just before the break, while Ezri Konsa and Ben White gave England a healthy lead before the hour mark.

La Roja fought back after that, though, with Elliot Anderson given his marching orders for a desperate foul on Lamine Yamal, and Mikel Oyarzabal calmly converted the resulting penalty.

Nico Williams pulled another back in the 75th minute, but Spain were unable to salvage a draw, though De la Fuente could not fault his players.

"I have nothing but words of pride and gratitude for the players and to value what has been done so far," the Spain manager said.

"All that is, whoever comes after me should improve upon it. I am proud of a fantastic journey, and all that lies ahead.

"You have to know how to win and how to lose, and for the first 30 minutes we were overwhelmed.

"[England] were better; they established their dominance. Then things changed; we had some chances, and at 0-3 down, we have to acknowledge what we did.

"But there are no excuses. Their goalkeeper was crucial. That 0-3 scoreline and the first half-hour really hampered us against a very strong opponent."

"Solo tengo palabras de agradecimiento para este equipo y nosotros somos iguales en la victoria y en la derrota".  "La derrota nos hace ver lo que hemos conseguido, pero esto sigue".  Luis de la Fuente, seleccionador nacional. #VamosEspaña | #NationsLeague

— Selección Española Masculina de Fútbol (@SEFutbol) November 15, 2026

Spain suffered only their second home loss across their last 41 such matches, coincidentally dating back to a 3-2 defeat to England in October 2018.

Sunday's loss also marked Spain's first in Madrid since February 1987, when they were likewise beaten by England.

Indeed, the defeat brought an end to Spain's 968-day unbeaten streak, which stretched back to a friendly defeat against Colombia in March 2024, with La Roja's 43-match run (excluding penalty shoot-outs) the longest by a European nation across all competitions.

"When matches don't start well, adverse situations accumulate," De la Fuente added. "[Marc] Pubill had an ankle problem, [Pau] Cubarsi had a muscle strain, [Martin] Zubimendi too…

"But we were able to recover, and the players gave their all.

"It's a shame we didn't at least get a draw, but I'm proud, and I insist again and again, of this fantastic group of players."

#1797. Man United's new boss contenders: Mauricio Pochettino tops the bookies' favourites ahead of Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann on 14-man list of top candidates

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:12 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 05:18 EST, 10 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino is the bookies' leading candidate to replace under-fire Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach should the latter get sacked.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport late on Monday night, Carrick is facing the sack during this November international break as a result of United's disastrous season so far.

Scrutiny on his role has intensified with the Red Devils now in the relegation zone despite salvaging a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino is currently in charge of the US national team, but his contract includes a £7million release clause. However, it is yet to be determined the true value of prising Pochettino out as that figure doesn't include buying out his backroom staff.

It is also believed within Pochettino's deal that there is another clause which would allow him to leave his US role for particular high-profile jobs, such as at Old Trafford.

And Betfair have the Argentine as the favourite to succeed Carrick should he be dismissed within the next fortnight before United travel to bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22.

Mauricio Pochettino is the bookmakers' favourite to become the next Man United head coach

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick is expected to get the sack after a poor start

As of 8.12am on Tuesday morning, they have him at 4/7 with out of work trio Eddie Howe (5/2), Julian Nagelsmann (5/1) and Didier Deschamps (15/2) the next favourites.

Antonio Conte and Aston Villa manager Unai Emery (both 9/1) follow the aforementioned quartet in the odds.

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler, Kieran McKenna, who worked with Carrick as an assistant manager to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, and ex-England manager Gareth Southgate are all 20/1.

Southgate's successor Thomas Tuchel is 28/1 alongside Diego Simeone, Sebastian Hoeness and Cesc Fabregas.

Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner is 33/1 too.

As Daily Mail Sport detailed, although it's understood that no final decision has been reached over Carrick's future and insiders say that speculation over his sacking is premature, the expectation within Old Trafford is that a new man will be in charge for the visit to Anfield a week on Sunday.

Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January and the former United midfielder was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

However, he has only won three of 15 games in all competitions. Breaking it down even further, the 45-year-old has overseen United's worst top-flight start since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago - with one victory in 10 matches.
